statement: Let W be any 4x4 phase-covariant Hermitian operator with correlated block H=t I_4+K, where K has zero diagonal and arbitrary complex Hermitian offdiagonals, and with diagonal coefficients d_ij on |ij> for i!=j. Let q_ij=sqrt(d_ij*d_ji) and q_*=min_(i<j)q_ij. If there is a perfect matching whose two q values both equal q_*, then every 2-block-positive W is decomposable. Uniform q_ij is a special case. No phase-balance or equal offdiagonal magnitude is assumed. In particular, under the common-correlated-diagonal hypothesis an indecomposable 2-block-positive phase-covariant candidate must have its minimum-q edges intersecting pairwise. The conclusion is a structured-family obstruction, not a solution of the original PPT/SN3 problem.
rank_two_spectral_test: 2-block positivity forces t>=0 and d_ij>=0. If K=0, W is PSD. Otherwise put lambda=-lambda_min(K)>0. Every 2x2 principal submatrix of K is [[0,K_ij],[conjugate(K_ij),0]], hence lambda>=|K_ij| for all pairs. Let z be a nonzero eigenvector with Kz=-lambda*z. On the perfect matching attaining q_* use the direct sum of two rank-one coefficient blocks with diagonal entries z_i; after optimizing their offdiagonal cost, the rank-two test gives 0<=z^*H z+2q_*(|z_i*z_j|+|z_k*z_l|). Since 2(|z_i*z_j|+|z_k*z_l|)<=||z||^2, this forces q_*>=lambda-t. Complex z phases are allowed: the offdiagonal rank-one determinant constraints fix only their products and the optimized cost depends on the moduli.
explicit_decomposition: If q_*>=lambda, for every pair set the offdiagonal of the |ij>,|ji> block B_ij equal to K_ij and its diagonals to d_ij,d_ji. Since |K_ij|<=lambda<=q_ij, B_ij>=0. Then W-B^Gamma has correlated block t I and zero offdiagonal-basis entries, hence is PSD. If q_*<lambda, instead choose the same diagonals and B_ij offdiagonal (q_*/lambda)K_ij. It is PSD because |(q_*/lambda)K_ij|<=q_*<=q_ij. Now W-B^Gamma has correlated block t I+(1-q_*/lambda)K, whose least eigenvalue is t-lambda+q_*>=0 by the rank-two test; every other entry vanishes. Thus W=A+B^Gamma. No 3x3 theorem or other external mathematical import is needed.
frustrated_nontrivial_example: Start with W0=(1/2)I+3 sum_i[|ii>]-[omega], omega=sum_i|ii>, which is 2-block positive by the two trace inequalities in frontier-20261028-matching-symmetric-witness-nogo-v1.json SHA256 374dab4d2e706a2bc5b037958b4c4b60763d58d303f9fe62e9694a26f2a7b765. Add the PSD correlated operator P with every correlated diagonal 1/5 and sole offdiagonal P_01=(2-20i)/101. Its 01 determinant is 1/2525>0. The resulting H has t=27/10, K_01=-(99+20i)/101, all other K_ij=-1, and every q_ij=1/2. The triangle product K_01*K_12*K_20 is non-real, hence frustrated; <omega|W|omega>=-586/505 and <02+20|W^Gamma|02+20>=-1, so W is neither PSD nor coPSD despite being 2-block positive. The theorem gives a mixed PSD+coPSD decomposition.

The 2-block validity of W0 and all-variable spectral/PSD argument are written proofs, not finite-sample inference.
